question: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&0\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}2&0&1\\ -1&3&4\\ 0&5&1\end{bmatrix}$ and $C=\begin{bmatrix}2\\ 3\\ 4\end{bmatrix},$ find ABC.
explanation:
**Step 1:** Multiply row matrix $A$ (order $1 \times 3$) with square matrix $B$ (order $3 \times 3$) to compute product matrix $AB$: $AB = \begin{bmatrix} 1(2)+(-1)(-1)+0(0) & 1(0)+(-1)(3)+0(5) & 1(1)+(-1)(4)+0(1) \end{bmatrix}$.
**Step 2:** Simplify the algebraic calculations to obtain the single horizontal row product vector: $AB = \begin{bmatrix} 2+1+0 & 0-3+0 & 1-4+0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -3 & -3 \end{bmatrix}$.
**Step 3:** Multiply this row matrix $AB$ (order $1 \times 3$) by the column matrix $C$ (order $3 \times 1$) to find the final scalar product matrix $ABC$: $ABC = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -3 & -3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} = [3(2) + (-3)(3) + (-3)(4)]$.
**Step 4:** Sum up the components: $[6 - 9 - 12] = [-15]$.
